decisionAtStake: Whether a TypeScript team should adopt decorator metadata on TS 5.9 today (vs. stay on legacy experimentalDecorators/emitDecoratorMetadata or wait), and which ecosystem pages they should monitor to know when that flips.
keyQuestion: As of October 2026, what stage has the TC39 Decorator Metadata proposal reached and how does TypeScript 5.9 actually support it, and which JavaScript-ecosystem documentation pages (TC39, TypeScript, MDN/BCD, caniuse, Node) currently and explicitly track that status?
assumptions: 'Current' means early October 2026, not TypeScript 5.9's release date; newer stable TS releases (5.9.x or 6.x) are in scope as context but the question is anchored to 5.9.

'Decorators metadata proposal' means the TC39 Decorator Metadata proposal built on the Stage 3 standard decorators — not the legacy tsc flags experimentalDecorators/emitDecoratorMetadata, though the interplay with those flags is part of the answer.

'JS-heavy documentation pages' means first-party ecosystem trackers — the tc39/proposal-decorator-metadata repo and tc39.es, TypeScript release notes/docs/tsconfig reference, MDN and MDN browser-compat-data, caniuse, Node.js docs — kept in English; framework docs (NestJS, Angular) and blog posts are excluded unless they turn out to be the only trackers.
'Tracks it' means the page actively states proposal stage, flag status, or engine/compiler support and gets updated — a page that merely mentions decorators once does not count.

The reader is a practicing TypeScript engineer or lead deciding adoption and monitoring; transpiler support (Babel/swc/esbuild) is secondary context, and no scholarly corpus is expected to be relevant.
whatWouldChangeTheAnswer: TC39 advancing Decorator Metadata to Stage 3 or 4, or any engine shipping it unflagged (Node LTS or a major browser), flips the verdict from 'experiment only, keep legacy flags' to 'adopt and migrate'.

TypeScript shipping a 5.9-era change — a new or renamed flag, altered metadata emission semantics, or deprecation of the experimental support — changes both the status answer and which docs pages are authoritative.

Finding that TS 5.9 introduced no decorator-metadata change at all (support frozen since the TS 5.2 implementation) reframes the question as a stale premise and shifts the authoritative pages to 5.2-era notes plus the TC39 repo.

Presence or absence of live MDN browser-compat-data / caniuse entries — and what status they show (no entry vs experimental vs shipped) — directly changes which pages count as trackers and the maturity verdict.
The proposal being renamed, merged into the main decorators proposal repo, or withdrawn would relocate where status is tracked and could invalidate the whole premise.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stage-2 limbo: as of Oct 2026 Decorator Metadata is still pre-Stage-3, TypeScript supports it only behind an unstable/experimental flag, and the only pages tracking it are the tc39 proposal README and TypeScript release notes — verdict: do not adopt yet.
hypotheses.killCriterion: TC39 readme/meeting notes or tc39.es showing Stage 3+ advancement, any unflagged engine shipment, or a live MDN/BCD/caniuse entry showing support.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stage 3 plateau: metadata sits at Stage 3 (decorators themselves have been Stage 3 since 2022) but remains flag-gated in TS 5.9 and unshipped in engines; trackers now include TypeScript's tsconfig/docs pages and possibly draft MDN BCD entries — verdict: safe to experiment behind flags, not to ship.
hypotheses.killCriterion: Evidence the proposal is still formally Stage 2 (proposal README or TC39 deck), or conversely that it reached Stage 4 / spec inclusion.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Shipped or Stage 4: by Oct 2026 Decorator Metadata hit Stage 4 or shipped in Node/browsers, TS 5.9-era compilers emit it without a legacy flag, and MDN plus caniuse carry live compat data — verdict: adopt and delete emitDecoratorMetadata.
hypotheses.killCriterion: MDN/BCD/caniuse still showing no support or experimental-only status, and the TC39 readme still listing it below Stage 4.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stale premise / no 5.9 delta: TypeScript 5.9 changed nothing about decorator metadata (implementation frozen since TS 5.2's Stage 2 support), so status is unchanged and the only true trackers are the TC39 proposal repo and TS 5.2-era documentation — the '5.9' framing is an artifact, not a development.
hypotheses.killCriterion: TypeScript 5.9 release notes, changelog, or PR history showing a decorator-metadata-specific change, or any TC39 status movement since the 5.2-era implementation.
